steps.text: Place the white sugar, brown sugar, corn syrup, and water in a saucepan over medium-high heat. Bring mixture to a boil, reduce heat to medium, cover pan, and simmer 8 minutes. Stir in maple extract and vanilla. Cool completely, then pour into glass jars, cover, and refrigerate.

raw_recipe.headline: Maple-Vanilla Syrup
raw_recipe.description: A brown sugar syrup flavored with maple and vanilla makes a delightful topping for pancakes, waffles, and French toast.
raw_recipe.name: Maple-Vanilla Syrup

Bring mixture to a boil, reduce heat to medium, cover pan, and simmer 8 minutes. Stir in maple extract and vanilla. Cool completely, then pour into glass jars, cover, and refrigerate.

review.reviewBody: If GodivaGirl didn't suggest Almond extract, I would've kept on rollin' by this recipe. (Never have maple flavoring, but I ALWAYS have Almond) and I also tossed in a shake of cinnamon. Although very runny, it's good. But, VERY VERY Sweet. Use just enough to soak into the pancake. **UPDATE** Made it again, cutting the sugar by 1/2 cup and using the Maple flavoring. Worth the trip to the store for the Maple Flavor!

I halved the white sugar,and water amount,and didn't add corn syrup[my oppinion of a nasty ingredient],I also didn't have brown sugar,so I omitted it.since I didn't have brown sugar,I "browned“ the white sugar in pan a few minutes,then added water,and at that moment,the sugar hardened and looked like rocks. But after it simmered 8 min, I took off the heat,and added flavorings. Let it cool a bit,and poured into a glass jar. Its really sweet,but yummy and natural tasting! I know my boys will love it on their pancakes!

I have made a variation of this for several years. First, the boiling time is too long- it only needs a minute or two. That's why people are ending up with candy. Also, using all white sugar and adding a tablespoon or so of molasses is the same concept but gives a deeper flavor. I also add butter flavoring to mine sometimes. My family likes it better than any store-bought!

Love this recipe. My very picky kids loved it too. It is a good base to creat your own. Added my own spin to it by adding 1/2 tsp sea salt, 1/2 tsp lemon extract, and a pinch of cinnamon. Ooooommmmgggggg!!! I am never buying store bought syrup again.

GREAT! I cut this in half and this was enough to fill just over half of a plastic syrup bottle. Way better than the store bought by a mile and super easy. I did add 1 tsp of butter extract along with the 1 tsp. of maple extract and 1 tsp. of vanilla. Good stuff.
Wonderful! I substituted the corner syrup with 3x the amount of organic pure maple syrup, and it's amazing!

I used this as my base idea for my whiskey syrup. With the hooch in place of the water, then a pinch of baking soda to keep it from crystalizing. I also used almond extract instead of maple flavor. Delicious! Tastes great and excellent consistency.
Instead of 1/2 cup of white sugar I used 1/4 cup of raw sugar to be more natural and less grams of sugar. It's AMAZING!!!

This recipe is our FAVORITE. Super easy to make and thickens up real nice in the fridge. Play around with different extracts. We have added butter extract, almond, and the maple it calls for. I also use real vanilla. Wish I could give it 10 stars!

k so I to tweeked this. listening to the advice of others I was able to solve the too-runny problem
I cut this recipe down to apotion of 6 (just me & my honey)
I used half cup each of water corn syrup & brown sugar. then just 2 tlbs of white sugar followed by a tlb of margarine as it was cooling 1/2 teasoop of vanilla 1/4 teaspoon of almond
this was excellent . honey did not even realize I created this my self

This recipe is what I grew up with. I rarely buy syrup. My mom's recipe didn't include corn syrup. I usually make it with maple and vanilla, however I have altered it in the past, including putting blueberries or strawberries in the the boiled mixture.
Made it according to the recipe, except, I added 4 tablespoons of butter. GREAT
I just made this syrup this morning. Unlike many other commenters, I didn’t fine it too runny at all. I brought a couple pancakes, along with some of the syrup, to my mom and she loved it.
We only use real maple syrup so I will just add real vanilla to it do not use corn syrup ever
Delicious! I cut down the regular sugar by 1/2 cup, and it turned out perfectly!

This came out great for me, but I cut the sugar by about 1/2 cup. It's not too thin at all, and once it cooled off, it thickened up. The flavor is good. I read a review that added butter flavoring, and I think that would be good in this too. I've never made syrup before, and this recipe made me want to try again. :) Thanks!
Awesome and thick

5.21.16 A bit too sweet for us (personal taste preference), but it still was enjoyed as a dipping sauce for french toast sticks. I could see substituting other extract flavors for the maple, just to provide some variety.
Really thick and sweet, but otherwise good. Maybe I need to add more water?
Great recipe. I added a little more vanilla to the recipe than it called for.
